assessment.reason: The study directly evaluates the feasibility and patient experience of routine EQ-5D-3L collection in oncology. The EuroQol Foundation explicitly supported the work through Grant #1456-PD.

studies.label: Pilot implementation and feasibility study of routine EQ-5D-3L collection in oncology
studies.family_rationale: The main contribution is an evaluation of the practical implementation, feasibility, and patient experience of routine EQ-5D-3L collection at an oncology centre.

items.statement: Interview participants generally described the questionnaire as simple, straightforward, quick to complete, and feasible to administer in the chemotherapy unit.
source: Full article, Results, Table 2 and Section 3.4

items.statement: Some patients considered the EQ-5D-3L too limited to represent the range of quality-of-life effects of cancer and treatment.
source: Full article, Results, Table 2 and Section 3.4

items.statement: Patients differed in their preferred paper or electronic format and suggested administration schedules ranging from every visit or every two to three weeks to the beginning, middle, and end of therapy.

items.statement: Implementation barriers included cancelled appointments, missed patients, patients being busy or asleep, short treatment durations, limited English fluency, and coordinator burden.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “The main weakness of this study”

items.statement: The authors concluded that routine EQ-5D-3L collection at the pilot oncology centre was feasible.
The authors stated that incorporating patient feedback provides actionable steps that can support larger-scale collection across Ontario cancer centres.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraphs on scale-up

items.statement: The authors considered EQ-5D-5L more appropriate than EQ-5D-3L for broader implementation because it can provide more precise HRQoL measurement.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “The main weakness of this study”

items.statement: The study was conducted at one oncology site, which limits generalizability to other sites and requires broader provincial confirmation.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “The main weakness of this study”

items.statement: The EQ-5D-3L questions were limited in their ability to capture the range of HRQoL experiences of patients undergoing cancer treatment.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “The main weakness of this study”

items.statement: The in-person study imposed a relatively high coordinator burden, with cumbersome recruitment and difficulty identifying appointment times for follow-up.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “The main weakness of this study”

items.statement: Measurement during chemotherapy could provide an inadequate snapshot because responses were sensitive to treatment timing and moment-to-moment changes in the patient’s condition.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “Completing the questionnaire in the chemotherapy unit”
